text: The second is a carrier protein, and glucose is our example. A glucose molecule outside fits into a binding site on the carrier. The carrier changes shape, so the binding site now faces the cytoplasm; the glucose is released, and the carrier returns to its first shape. In our facilitated-diffusion example, the carrier moves glucose down its concentration gradient without ATP. It can carry either way, just more often from the side with more glucose. One caution: needing a protein does not, by itself, fix the direction or the energy source of every glucose transporter.
